name: resurrection
lore:
To reach beyond the Veil and pluck a soul from the Gray is the ultimate defiance of entropy. Shaping this magic feels like grasping a heavy, golden chain submerged in deep water; it requires a grueling exertion of will to haul the departed spirit back against the relentless current of the afterlife.

Visually, the spell manifests as a gentle, amber radiance that seeps into the remains like warm honey. Wounds do not merely close; they vanish as the Weave re-knits the very history of the flesh. The final transition is marked by a sharp, crystalline chime—the sound of a soul snapping back into its mortal vessel.

Chronicles attribute this miracle to Aethelgard the Mourner. It is said she spent forty days in the Silent Halls, weaving her own silver hair into a tether to lead her fallen king home. She did not steal him from Death; she simply convinced the Grave that his story remained unfinished. Tread carefully: such power demands a diamond of peerless clarity, for only the purest stone can anchor a wandering spirit to our fragile realm.
